title: VS Code Examples
description: Small VS Code examples from the lessons. Each example links back to its explanation and practice task.

examples.title: An editor helps you write files
examples.description: Visual Studio Code is a code editor. It helps you read and change files, but it is not the same thing as a browser or every language's runtime.
examples.code:
Editor: write index.html
Browser: display index.html
Separate runtime: needed for languages such as Python

examples.title: Open a practice folder
examples.description: Opening a folder gives the editor a workspace for related files. Use a new folder made only for learning.

examples.title: Use the Command Palette
examples.description: The Command Palette searches editor actions by name. It is useful when you do not remember a menu location.
examples.code:
Open the Command Palette
Search: Format Document
Read the command name before choosing it

examples.title: Save and recognise file types
examples.description: A file extension helps the editor choose language support. Saving changes writes them to disk; an unsaved tab can differ from the saved file.
examples.code:
index.html -> HTML
style.css -> CSS
notes.txt -> plain text

examples.title: Search within a file
examples.description: Find locates matching text in the current file. Check match-case and whole-word settings when results seem surprising.
examples.code:
Text: Moon moon moonlight
Search: moon
Match case on: lowercase matches only
Whole word on: excludes moonlight

examples.title: Search across the project
examples.description: Workspace search finds text in several files. Review the included and excluded paths before trusting the result.
examples.code:
Search target: club-site files
Query: Reading club
Possible matches: index.html and notes.txt

examples.title: Replace with a preview
examples.description: Replace changes text. Review each match or the preview before applying many changes at once.
examples.code:
Old label: Save book
New label: Bookmark book
Review: check every matched file before replacing

examples.title: Formatting keeps layout consistent
examples.description: A formatter adjusts layout such as indentation. It should preserve the intended program behaviour. The formatter used depends on the language and setup.
examples.code:
Before: const score={value:8};
After:  const score = { value: 8 };

examples.title: Workspace settings
examples.description: Workspace settings apply to the project. A .vscode/settings.json file can record a few agreed editor choices.

examples.title: The integrated terminal
examples.description: The integrated terminal is a real shell inside the editor window. Its commands can change files just like any other terminal.
examples.code:
Read the current directory
Run a harmless version command if the tool is installed
Example: git --version

examples.title: Extensions and workspace trust
examples.description: Extensions add editor features. Workspace Trust helps decide whether code in a folder may activate potentially risky features.
examples.code:
New downloaded project
First: read its files in a restricted state
Then: trust only when you understand the source and needed actions

examples.title: Debug one step at a time
examples.description: A debugger can pause a supported program and let you inspect values. A breakpoint marks a place to pause. Setup depends on the language runtime.
examples.code:
Breakpoint before: total = price * count
Inspect: price is 3, count is 2
Step over: total becomes 6
